newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee rises despite overseas dlr gains.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee rises despite overseas dlr gains.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee remained strong against the dollar in early Friday morning trade, despite the dollar gaining overseas, dealers said.

At 0500 GMT, the rupee was at 58.40 to the dollar after opening at 58.58 and moving to 58.70. On Thursday, it closed at 58.45. The Central Bank, going by the international strengthening of the greenback, pushed it up by 4.5 local cents and fixed buying and selling at 58.1947 and 59.3703.
"The dollar shot up to 58.70 soon after the Central Bank range was announced and speculators began to get active," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.

Dealers said the dollar was unlikely to rise given the Central Bank's positive stand towards the local currency this week and lack of commercial demand. "Up to now we haven't seen any commercial demand, which is probably why the dollar is not gaining," said a Panasia Asia Bank.
Some dealers, however, say signals from the Central Bank were the main reason for the dollar's slump in the local market.
Overnight call money rates, which were volatile due to a lack of sellers, were at 15 percent after opening at 13 and going to a high of 16 perecent, dealers said.
